bad.title: A plain tile with the quantity
bad.text: Nothing hints that a tap adds one and only a long press takes one away.

bad.title: Each try to lower it adds one
bad.text: People tapping to get back to 1 watch €24 climb to €36, then €48.

good.title: A − button takes one away
good.text: The stepper people know from other shops, so 1 is one click away.

good.title: A + button beside it
good.text: Both directions are in view, and screen readers announce Remove one and Add one.

good.title: Stops at 1, and says so
good.text: The − button turns off at 1, so people know they’ve reached the floor.

bad.title: Enter adds a line in the cell
bad.text: Type 900 and press Enter, and the cursor stays in Rent on a new line.

bad.title: The total breaks to #ERROR
bad.text: Rent ends up holding 900 and 450 on two lines, so the sum fails.

good.title: Enter saves and moves to Food
good.text: People type down the column the way they do in any spreadsheet.

good.title: The total updates on each Enter
good.text: 900, then 450, gives 1350, with no stray lines in any cell.

bad.title: No Save button, no status
bad.text: The bar shows only “Gift ideas”, so people can’t tell if a change was kept.

bad.title: Ctrl+S does nothing
bad.text: The habit people bring from other apps meets silence, and the doubt stays.
bad.wait: Press Ctrl+S in the note to see this.

good.title: “Saved” in the bar
good.text: It turns to “Saving…” while people type, then back, so they can see it worked.

good.title: Ctrl+S explains the new way
good.text: The usual shortcut still works, and the hint says notes save on their own.
good.wait: Press Ctrl+S in the note to see this.

bad.title: A 12-pixel target on each photo
bad.text: The ✕ is the whole button, so a near miss lands on the photo.

bad.title: Every miss opens the photo
bad.text: The counter shows how often people miss, and each miss is a detour.

good.title: Same icon, 32-pixel button
good.text: The ✕ still looks small, but the area that takes the click is much bigger.

good.title: Misses stay at 0
good.text: Three blurry photos take three clicks, even with a finger or a shaky hand.

bad.title: Save in the top corner
bad.text: From Postcode, the pointer has to cross the whole form to reach it.

bad.title: Postcode is where people finish
bad.text: The last field sits at the far end of the form from Save.

good.title: Save right under Postcode
good.text: A short move down from the last field, in the order people read the form.

good.title: The pointer is already here
good.text: After the postcode, the next step is just below, not across the screen.

bad.title: Reply is a tiny target
bad.text: The action people use most is a small button tucked in the corner.

bad.title: Delete touches Reply
bad.text: Same size, 2 pixels apart, so a slip meant for Reply deletes the email.

bad.title: Gone for good, no undo
bad.text: One slip costs the whole email, with no way back.

good.title: Reply is the big button
good.text: It spans the width under the email, right where people finish reading.

good.title: Delete sits apart, in the bar
good.text: A trash icon at the far end of the bar, nowhere near Reply.

good.title: Undo for six seconds
good.text: If a slip does happen, Undo brings the email back.
good.wait: Press the trash icon to see this.

bad.title: 22 cities in no order
bad.text: Madrid, Oslo, Athens… Lisbon is number 15, so people read down until they find it.
bad.wait: Open the list to see this.

bad.title: Seconds spent scanning
bad.text: The demo times the pick, so people can compare it with the other side.
bad.wait: Pick a city to see this.

good.title: Type “lis” to narrow it
good.text: The search box has focus when the list opens, and three letters leave only Lisbon.
good.wait: Open the list to see this.

good.title: Recent trips first
good.text: Lisbon and Porto sit at the top, so a repeat trip is one click.
good.wait: Open the list to see this.

good.title: The rest, sorted A to Z
good.text: People who don’t search can still guess where their city sits.
good.wait: Open the list to see this.

bad.title: Four gray buttons in a row
bad.text: Save as copy, Don’t save, Save and Cancel look alike, so people read every one.
bad.wait: Press Close document to see this.

bad.title: Don’t save sits next to Save
bad.text: With equal weight, it’s easy to throw away the edits by mistake.
bad.wait: Press Close document to see this.

bad.title: Focus lands on Save as copy
bad.text: Pressing Enter right away makes a copy, not the save people wanted.
bad.wait: Press Close document to see this.

good.title: Save is the one primary button
good.text: It sits last and has focus, so Enter does the usual thing.
good.wait: Press Close document to see this.

good.title: Don’t save is a quieter button
good.text: Still easy to find, but it no longer competes with Save.
good.wait: Press Close document to see this.

good.title: Rare choices are plain text
good.text: Save as copy and Cancel step back, so the eye goes to Save first.
good.wait: Press Close document to see this.

bad.title: Three options, nothing more
bad.text: Copy link, Send to… and Save to device. Full-size download was cut.

bad.title: Save to device shrinks the photo
bad.text: It saves at 1600 px, and nothing else offers the original.

good.title: The common three stay in view
good.text: Most people still pick from the same short list as before.

good.title: More options, with a count
good.text: The 3 tells people there’s more, without showing it all the time.

good.title: Full size is one click in
good.text: Download original (24 MP) saves the photo at 6000 × 4000.
good.wait: Press More options to see this.

bad.title: Export, with no size choice
bad.text: It always makes a 1080 px file, and nothing on screen offers another.

bad.title: The print shop needs 3,000 px
bad.text: The photo is 4032 px wide, so the app throws away what the task needs.

bad.title: A dead end after Export
bad.text: “There’s no way to pick another size.” People can’t finish the task here.

good.title: Export is still one click
good.text: People who just want to share get the 1080 px default, as before.

good.title: More options next to Export
good.text: The size choice is one click away for the people who need it.

good.title: Full size, labeled for printing
good.text: “Good for printing” tells people which size suits the print shop.
good.wait: Press More options to see this.

bad.title: One exact format, spelled out
bad.text: +447700900123 with no spaces is how the system stores it, not how people write it.

bad.title: A vague error for a real number
bad.text: The number is right, but people have to retype it in the app’s format.
bad.wait: Type 07700 900 123 and press Save to see this.

good.title: Help says why, not how
good.text: “We’ll text you when the parcel is close” explains what the number is for.

good.title: Any common format works
good.text: Spaces, a leading 0 or 0044 are all fine. The product tidies them up.

good.title: Saved as +44 7700 900123
good.text: The app adds the country code and spacing, so it works on the first try.
good.wait: Type 07700 900 123 and press Save to see this.

bad.title: Tested with one sample photo
bad.text: One 1 MB sample.jpg is nothing like what people’s phones make.

bad.title: Error 415 on the HEIC photo
bad.text: An iPhone’s usual format fails with a code people can’t act on.
bad.wait: Press Upload 4 files to see this.

bad.title: Only 1 of 4 uploaded
bad.text: The errors don’t say what to do, so people try again or give up.
bad.wait: Press Upload 4 files to see this.

good.title: Tested with real phone files
good.text: HEIC photos, odd names and big videos were part of the test, not a surprise.

good.title: The HEIC photo becomes a JPG
good.text: People never see the format problem. The product converts it.
good.wait: Press Upload 4 files to see this.

good.title: All 4 uploaded
good.text: The 1.8 GB video goes up in parts, so a big file just takes longer.
good.wait: Press Upload 4 files to see this.
